MODERN_TANK_PORT_REDRAW_COUPLER_FLOATS.note: Lower-lane W and E couplers sit flush on the drawn camlock fittings on all three tanks (tall, IBC, XTall), with no stub or gap. But A2 asks for BOTH lanes, and no capture lays a hose to the upper-lane fittings (they show bare). Needed: the same three W/E shots with hoses also laid to the upper lane (dz +0.5). The C3_north shots are a rusty tank, not a Modern one, so they say nothing here.

TANK_FLANGE_FIX_HOVERS_MID_PIPE.note: C3 north: the flange collar sits right under the tank skid where pipe 17,43 meets it; no flange mid-pipe. On map R C1 the west pipe ends in a flange ring at the tank body and the trunk collar touches the skid's SE corner. Minor: a slightly paler section on the vertical pipe just below the skid looks like a texture seam, not a fitting.

TANK_STUB_HUNT_POINTS_AT_NOTHING.note: The pipe-to-reel link leaves the pipe with an elbow, runs east and turns down into the top of reel o1. Nothing under the tank ends in air.

C1_CORD_REWIRE_BATTERY_GOES_SKINNY_DIPPI.note: The cord does stay over land, but about 1 cell east of the bank pump (35,73) it draws a closed loop around the pump's pipe with a kinked V where it meets itself, and a separate strand goes from the pump's west fitting out and back. The pump also still shows the yellow no-power bolt, so the cord reads as not reaching the pump.

C1_TANK_STUB_PRUNE_PIPE_TO_NOWHERE.note: No dead-end L under the tall tank. The trunk leaves the skid's SE corner with a collar and bends south, and the incoming west pipe ends in a flange ring at the tank body.

CREEK_STATIONS_REDESIGN_FORDED_A_PUDDLE.note: R1 and R2 both run N-S from the grassy north bank to the dirt south bank across the full river width; neither follows an inlet. R1 has no crossing marker drawn (it is a current crossing), so only its framing shows it. An unidentified white dome object sits in the water at R1's north bank (see other_findings).

FORD_STONES_REDRAW_LOOK_LIKE_A_SMUDGE.note: No longer a dark smear: at play zoom it reads as a chain of pale flat stones with darker wet pebble clusters. Caveat: the pale segments are smooth, elongated sandy ovals, close to a sand path, and the 1-cell column has hard straight vertical edges against the water. The south-bank shoreline also steps sharply at the ford column.

PUMPSTATION_SOUTH_PORT_REDRAW_ALMOST_THE.note: On both Kludged and Repaired, the hose camlock meets the drawn dark collar at the bottom centre of the art with no gap. Separate from the port: on the Kludged station the hose's straight lead-out continues about 0.4 cell past the point where its curve leaves sideways, a short dead-end hose tail (the detour around the canal scene).

other_findings.seen: The hose's drawn curve clips the wall's bottom-left corner (it passes over the wall's south end). This agrees with the filed CENTRE_CELLS_FIX_WALK_THROUGH_WALLS. Several dark blurry cross-shaped blotches in the terrain (top right, bottom right, bottom left) look like stale shadows or stains with no building.
Dead-end hose tail below the bend (see the PUMPSTATION note).
A plain white dome with a black outline and no texture detail sits in the water near the north bank. Possibly a missing or flat texture; identify it.
The pole span over the ditch draws as a saturated bright-red, almost straight line. The C1 sign promises a sag over the ditch; check that red is the intended cable colour.
One vertical run between two red reels alternates hose (beige) / pipe (copper) / hose. Confirm it is drawn intentionally (bleed-well feed), not a pipe sitting under a hose.
Bank pump shows the no-power bolt (see the C1_CORD note). The Kludged and Repaired stations also show it, which is expected for unpowered god builds.
